A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dyn-VQA dataset and OmniSearch framework. Their text, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content and v1 Table 14 to v3 Table 16.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, human performance, retrieval ablations, cost measurements and dataset analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports token costs by question category and latency measurements in Appendix D.3.

M1.justification: The planner, retriever and sub-question solver, GPT-4V prompting, and Qwen-VL training procedure remain unchanged. The added CoT discussion explains positioning; the corrected sub-question tag in Table 10 is a typographical correction rather than an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,452-question bilingual Dyn-VQA dataset, other VQA benchmarks and training sources. Appendix D.3 analyzes existing answer-update categories and model configurations without adding datasets or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same original models, heuristic mRAG methods, commercial search engines and human baseline. Newly cited CoT, ReAct and multimodal reasoning work are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix D.3 adds evaluation of average per-question search, inference and total latency, alongside token-cost breakdowns by answer-update frequency. Existing accuracy metrics, training settings and evaluation cutoff remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish reruns of earlier experiments.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.3 examines how question category affects token consumption and how planner/solver configurations affect latency. Earlier retrieval-content ablations, top-k sensitivity, metric consistency, domain analyses and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Annotation agreement and metric-correlation reporting remain unchanged, and the new efficiency tables introduce no uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Existing performance results remain unchanged, including Table 4 overall scores of 50.03 for OmniSearch (GPT-4V) and 41.20 for OmniSearch (Qwen-VL-Chat). New Tables 14–15 add category-specific token costs and reported total latencies of 31.5, 27.6, 22.2 and 26.2 seconds for four existing configurations.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations are added or revised. The new CoT discussion is conceptual, and the computational-cost additions are empirical.

C1.justification: The introduction qualifies the claim of being the first multimodal retrieval agent for VQA by adding 'with self-adaptive planning and scalable submodules.' This modestly narrows that novelty statement; the dataset, framework and effectiveness contributions otherwise remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix D.3 adds explanations linking token consumption to retrieval steps and GPT-4V verification behavior, and interprets solver substitution as offloading computation. It also discusses latency's dependence on system configuration. Existing long-context and visual-grounding limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v1 provides a repository address for the promised code/data release; v3 removes the address while retaining the future-release promise. Table 10 corrects a malformed prompt tag. Training hyperparameters and hardware disclosures in Appendix C.3 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds six cited works, including CoT, ReAct and multimodal reasoning research. Section 4.2 adds a CoT distinction, and Appendix C.4 credits ReAct and Chen et al. for prompt inspiration. These are focused additions rather than a wholesale repositioning.

P1.justification: The introduction expands explanations of non-adaptive and overloaded retrieval with concrete examples. v3 also adds the CoT paragraph and Appendix D.3, edits the author line and corrects a prompt typo. Most prose and the overall section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds two computational-cost tables and renumbers the existing cross-dataset table from 14 to 16. Figures 2–3 are resized, and some table/text placement changes. Existing figures and tables otherwise retain their content and basic design.

improvement.justification: v1 already reports aggregate costs; v3 modestly improves practical assessment through category-specific token costs and latency, while adding useful prior-work attribution. These gains are limited by removal of the repository address and an inconsistency in new Table 15: the first row's 14.1-second search and 18.4-second inference times sum to 32.5, but its total is 31.5. The additions provide a limited net benefit while leaving the core empirical evidence unchanged.
